tool_args.old_string: For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. \citet{edwards_lessler_naimi2021} showed dependent misclassification can bias in either direction, a concern that also drives mediation analyses with mismeasured mediators~\cite{valeri_vanderweele2013}.
tool_args.new_string: For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, with \citet{neuhaus1999} quantifying the attenuation and efficiency loss in binary regression under known misclassification rates; but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. \citet{edwards_lessler_naimi2021} showed dependent misclassification can bias in either direction, and \citet{shu_yi2019a, shu_yi2019b} develop weighted estimators that jointly handle mismeasured covariates and misclassified outcomes under IPW---a concern that also drives mediation analyses with mismeasured mediators~\cite{valeri_vanderweele2013}.

tool_args.new_string: For correction, PPI++~\cite{angelopoulos2023} and DSL~\cite{egami_hinck_stewart_wei2023} are topology-agnostic; \citet{zrnic_candes2024} extend PPI to gold-free settings, \citet{cadei2025} adapt prediction-powered estimation to treatment-effect targets via a deconfounded risk objective, and \citet{gligoric2025} leverage LLM confidence scores.
